aurelia_explorer.introduction: Explore the 8-bit platform that starts the Logix story. From its processor to its peripheral ecosystem, one connected system at a time.
aurelia_explorer.context: Logix launches Aurelia as a complete personal-computing platform: hardware, enhanced CP/M, AION applications, developer programs, support and the Computer Academy.

timeline.title: NCC 1978
timeline.description: Aurelia launches with FlexiBUS, enhanced CP/M 1.4 and the separately offered BPI business suite.

timeline.title: NCC 1979
timeline.description: Microsoft BASIC for Aurelia premieres alongside the Apple II interoperability products.

timeline.title: COMDEX 1979
timeline.description: Aurelia+ arrives alongside Pulse and Abacus 2.0; Monitor II options become available.

timeline.title: Software direction
timeline.description: Artemis becomes the primary AION software platform; Aurelia receives maintenance and simplified refreshes.

timeline.title: NCC 1981
timeline.description: An optional network adapter and CP/M upgrade add business networking.

notes.hardware: AION system controller contains DMA, bank control and independent system refresh. Video uses 16 KiB DRAM plus exclusive 1 KiB sprite SRAM.
notes.peripherals: Compatible choices, not simultaneous port occupancy. Later accessories show their introduction dates; they were not included at the original launch.
notes.software: Explore system internals, the Business Tools cartridge and independent software offerings. Introduction dates are shown; later editions are not implied at launch.
notes.memory: Logical CPU windows map physical banks. DMA latches physical banks; all installed DRAM is refreshed. Sprite SRAM uses separate video ports and is not application RAM.
notes.bundles: Bundle decomposition. Existing offers and proposed packages are labeled separately. Listed dates prevent later software from being implied at launch; prices are not assumed.
notes.portability: Shared application code and C APIs; separate target binaries, startup code and libraries. Optional emulator/debugging features are not guaranteed launch components.

artemis_explorer.context: Artemis uses paired 16-bit RAM modules on a 32-bit memory bus. PRO uses the same high-density module family with larger populations. Native ERA applications use AIONix; the optional Z80 card remains a separate execution path qualified only for Artemis.
artemis_explorer.memory_note: Functional address map. The selected replaceable video card contains its controller, 16 or 32 KiB display DRAM, independent 1 KiB sprite SRAM and internal buffers. Host MMU, DMA and system refresh remain outside the card. Numeric apertures are not yet assigned.
artemis_explorer.ram_note: Choose an explicit matched-bank population. Low- and high-density configurations with the same capacity are distinct. Expanded populations and 1 MiB board capacity are design targets pending timing, loading and power qualification; they are not extra shipping bundles.
artemis_explorer.bundle_note: Bundle contents follow the selected catalog offer and are independent of the exploratory RAM and networking controls. Items absent from the bundle record are not assumed to be included.

notes.hardware: Select a block to inspect the processor, RAM, custom chipset, storage and expansion interfaces. Lines show functional relationships, not a wiring or bus-timing specification.
notes.peripherals: Compatible devices are grouped by interface. Dashed connections denote optional devices; a monitor listed as a bundle option is included only in bundles naming that monitor. Introduction dates are shown for later offerings.
notes.software: Explore the native AIONix services, Business Tools, compatible software and C development tools. The optional Z80 module is distinct from native ERA recompilation.
notes.memory: Follow virtual addressing through the MMU to physical memory resources. Select RAM capacity to inspect module population. No undefined address ranges are invented.
notes.bundles: Select an offer to see its computer configuration, devices, software and services. Planned availability remains explicitly labeled.
